answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may submit jobs, then slash that stake when independent audits prove its outputs were fraudulent. This does not make identities unique: an attacker can still create many, but every one must tie up capital and risk losing it. A vine of cheap accounts therefore cannot amplify influence for free; the fable of effortless Sybil power breaks when each false persona must bear an onyx-sized bond and real audit exposure.
